name: Raynham
blurb: Raynham and the surrounding Route 44 corridor are home to a dense mix of home service businesses competing for the same searches. We've built websites and CRM systems for HVAC and contracting companies based right in town.

name: Lynn
blurb: Lynn's mix of dense residential neighborhoods and older housing stock keeps hardscaping, tree service, and remodeling crews busy year-round — and makes local search visibility especially competitive.

name: Rehoboth
blurb: Rehoboth's larger residential lots make it a strong market for hardscaping, patios, and outdoor living projects — the kind of work that sells on photos and a fast-loading project gallery.

name: South Yarmouth
blurb: Cape Cod's seasonal population swings mean local service businesses in South Yarmouth need marketing that ramps up ahead of summer and a CRM that keeps second-home clients on the books year after year.

name: Plymouth
blurb: Plymouth's mix of historic homes and new construction keeps carpentry, painting, and remodeling contractors busy with two very different kinds of projects — and two very different kinds of customers to market to.

name: Northborough
blurb: Northborough sits at the center of a MetroWest market with strong demand for both residential and commercial glass and glazing work, from storefront installs to custom shower enclosures.

name: Harwich
blurb: Harwich's classic-car and craftsman community supports specialty trades that sell on reputation and visible quality of work — exactly the kind of business a portfolio-driven website is built for.

name: Rockland
blurb: Rockland and the surrounding South Shore towns are steady territory for masonry and hardscape contractors, with enough new construction and renovation work to keep a well-marketed crew booked solid.

name: Beverly
blurb: Beverly and the North Shore combine coastal weather exposure with older housing stock — a market where masonry, exterior, and restoration businesses stay busy if they can be found by the right searches.

name: Derry
blurb: Derry anchors a fast-growing corner of southern New Hampshire where masonry, tree work, and remodeling businesses are competing against a wave of new residents searching for local contractors online for the first time.
